definition: Dot matrix printing uses arrays of dots to form text and graphics, usually through pins striking an inked ribbon against paper.
entry_text: Dot matrix printing uses arrays of dots to form text and graphics, usually through pins striking an inked ribbon against paper.
example: A shop prints a delivery slip and its carbon-copy duplicates on an impact dot matrix printer.
label: Dot matrix printing
sense_note: Interpreted as the familiar impact printer technology.
